There is no other source. Although in other places, incarnations are called God because of their actions,
but they are not called the complete Supreme Being anywhere. In this verse, the word 'Swayam' indicates their superiority as the ultimate merit. The ultimate refuge, Krishna, is one and indivisible. He has expanded himself in various parts, arts,
and particles, as self-form, self-illuminating, that one soul, the manifestation of glory and splendor.
He has done it in the name of Avesh and Jiva; all these are endowed with countless powers that are entirely suitable for the forms and personalities related to it. The scholars of spirituality have, in the final
aspect, studied Krishna with utmost care and have described his 64 main qualities.
In all the parts or categories of God, only a certain percentage of these qualities is found. But in Shri Krishna,
these qualities are found 100%.
From self-illumination and that one soul to the categories of incarnation,
their personal expansions, which are all Vishnu elements, up to 93 percent of these divine qualities
are found. In Shivji, who is neither an incarnation, nor passion, nor comes between these two,
in them, approximately 84 percent of virtues are found. But in organisms with different stages of life,
these traits are found up to 78 percent. In this physical world, in the bound state, these qualities are very
found in small quantities, and in pure beings, their quantity may be different. In living beings,
the most complete being is Brahma, who is the presiding deity of a universe. In them, up to 78 percent of these properties
are found in full quantity. In other deities, the amount of these qualities decreases, and in humans,
then very little quantity is found. The standard of completeness of human life is that they increase these qualities
up to 78 percent in full quantity. In a living being, qualities like Shiva, Vishnu, or Lord Krishna can never come.
Any living being, having fully developed 78 percent of its qualities, can attain divinity,
but it can never become Shiva, Vishnu, or Krishna. Yes, in chronological order, it can become Brahma.
Those divine beings, who are residents of the planets of the spiritual sky, are eternally companions of God in various spiritual planets like Haridham

दोनों के लिए कल्पनामात्र है । बद्धजीवों के वर्तमान स्वरूप भी वास्तविक नहीं हैं। निष्कर्ष यह है

There is no difference between their body and soul, as there is in a bound soul. The concept of the cosmic form is only for the newly initiated
worshippers. For them, the physical, immense form is presented, the explanation of which
will be in the second why. In the form of Virat, the physical form of various folk is imagined as their feet, hands, etc. Actually, all such descriptions are for the novice. They
cannot think beyond the substance. The physical perception of God is not counted in the list of their real
forms. In the form of the Supreme Being, God resides within every physical form,
even within the atoms, but the external physical form is merely an imagination for both God and the living being. The current forms of the bound organisms are also not real. The conclusion is
that the concept of God's cosmic form is imaginary. God and the living being are both living souls.
And their original body is spiritual (chinmaya). Just as the clouds are to the sky, the earth is to the rain.

Clouds and dust are carried away by the wind, but the few say that the sky

covering of the body or the subtle mind of the living being, but we cannot see the
spiritual spark within the body.

the presence of the living being has to be accepted. Similarly, those who want to see God with their current
physical eyes or with physical senses, they are advised to meditate on the cosmic form.
For example, when a person sits in his car and goes somewhere, which

the President sits in his special car and goes somewhere, we say, '* There he is, the President.'" At that
time, we identify the car with the President. Similarly, those ignorant people who
want to have a direct vision of God without necessary qualifications, they are shown that
the gigantic physical universe is the form of God, although God is everywhere, inside and out. In this context, the example of clouds in the sky and the blue sky can be taken.
Although,
the blue of the sky and the sky are different, but we consider the color of the sky to be blue. But this is only a general perception of the alpannam.

Beyond this gross concept of form, there is another subtle concept of form, which has no
shape and which is invisible, unheard, and unexpressed. The form of life is beyond this
subtlety, otherwise it would not have to be born again and again. Meaning: Just as the gross visible world is conceived as the immense body of God,
so too is the subtle body of His, which cannot be seen, nor
heard or manifested. But in reality, all these gross or subtle concepts of the body are related to living beings.
The soul has its own spiritual form, which is beyond this
gross physical or subtle psychological existence. As soon as a living being abandons this visible gross body,
it stops performing gross body and psychological actions. In fact,
we say that the living being is gone, because it is neither visible nor audible. Even up to here,
when the soul is in deep sleep, then the gross body does not function, so we know
that because of breathing, it is inside the body. Therefore, the departure of a living being from the body (death)
does not mean that the soul does not exist. It is here, otherwise why is there rebirth again? The conclusion that came out is that God remains eternally present in his divine form, which is neither gross nor subtle like a living being. His body can never be compared to the gross and subtle bodies of a living being. All such concepts of God's body are imaginary.
Of the soul,
It has its eternal spiritual form, which remains bound only because of its physical impurities.
